summary: On 30 June 2026 the FCA and the Bank of England published a joint approach describing how they, and other authorities where relevant, will regulate systemic stablecoin issuers in the UK. It sets out how supervisory responsibility is split: the Bank leads on prudential matters such as backing assets, capital and failure arrangements, the FCA leads on conduct, consumer protection and financial crime, and some areas overlap. An issuer starts out under FCA-only supervision and moves to joint FCA/Bank of England regulation once HM Treasury formally recognises it as systemic, a designation assessed by factors including transaction volumes, substitutability and interconnectedness. The authorities describe the approach as aiming to give firms clarity and predictability as the market develops.
title: FCA and the Bank of England set out approach to joint regulation of systemic stablecoin issuers
why_it_matters: The FCA supervises a UK stablecoin issuer on its own until HM Treasury formally designates it systemic, at which point the Bank of England -- the UK's central bank -- joins as a second, financial-stability-focused regulator alongside the FCA. It shows UK stablecoin oversight is designed to intensify as a stablecoin grows in size and importance, rather than staying fixed with one regulator throughout.
